Yes this seems a little bit confused if users pass in `false` but we will still respect the `ctx.bufferred_proxying`.
My intention was to reduce the read of `ctx`, because local variable is faster than `ctx`, and when invoking `get_raw_body` inside `get_body` I could just pass in the `ctx.bufferd_proxying` we've read already.
I think we can revert the `get_raw_body` change, and inside the `get_body` function, just replace the `get_raw_body` call with `return ctx.buffered_body or ""`, because we already do the `check_phase` and `ctx.buffered_proxying` check, what do you think?

discussion_comments.comment_body: Yes, I would revert these PDK API changes (where we add new parameters). Not worth it, and paints us in a corner.

What we need is to cover `google.proto.any` to match https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/proto3#json 

It is not possible without knowing descriptors in advance. I understood the conclusion from related discussions
- https://github.com/Kong/kong/issues/7710
- https://github.com/Kong/kong/issues/8725

is: _support for dynamic reflection is expensive_.

This extra field does it statically while avoiding digression of `protojson` from its sister implementations:
- https://pkg.go.dev/google.golang.org/protobuf/encoding/protojson
- https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/csharp/class/google/protobuf/json-formatter
- https://developers.google.com/protocol-buffers/docs/reference/cpp/google.protobuf.util.json_util

I did not figure any better way to support `any` type. I would be happy to support it in any better "kong-friendly" way.
This also requires an entry in the changelog.

Notice that adding fields to `schema.lua` means we also need to add a field in `kong/clustering/compat/removed_fields.lua`. ([schema-change-noteworthy](https://github.com/Kong/kong/labels/schema-change-noteworthy))
If you're not sure how to do it, please let me know and I'll do it for you.

--Green Hat Idea-- 
What do you think about switching this from `keep_incoming_path` being a boolean to an enum like: `incoming_path_strategy`: `One.of({'preserve', 'combine', 'ignore'})` or something similar? At the beginning we could start with `preserve` and `ignore` (`ignore` being the default).

I'm trying to look a bit ahead and see if a boolean won't limit us to much. At the same time it might introduce flexibility where we don't need it since combining incoming path with the one defined above would require us to answer questions about precedence etc.

Oh.. I've just noticed that this was your original idea https://github.com/Kong/kong/pull/13900#discussion_r1852046997 ! I've re-read the discussion you had with @kikito. Let's keep it simple then as it's not been requested.

@nowNick I initially had `combine` as an option, but removed it due to complexity + lack of use case.

I think I'd recommend additional parameters in the future anyway as `combine` can be one of multiple states:

* merge paths (location first)
* merge paths (request first)
* merge query (keep all)
* merge query (prefer location)
* merge query (prefer request)

So we'd end up with `keep_incoming_path: true` and `path_strategy: location_first` + `query_strategy: prefer_location`

`path_strategy` and `query_strategy` would only be valid with `keep_incoming_path: true`
